title: HoardItem
description: A single record in the Hoard. Append-heavy, searchable, indexable, not required to be tidy. Hoard answers the question: what should not be lost, even if it is not active? It protects against loss. Hoard files SHOULD be stored as JSONL where each line validates against this schema.

id.description: Globally stable id. ULID or UUID recommended; kebab-case allowed for hand-curated entries.

captured_at.description: When the item was captured into the Hoard.

occurred_at.description: When the underlying event actually happened, if different from captured_at.

content.description: Primary content. Plain text or markdown. For binary artifacts use 'attachment' instead.

attachment.description: Pointer to a file held outside the Hoard index (image, audio, pdf, raw transcript).

area.description: Lifecycle classification — which slice of life this item belongs to. PER FOLLOW-UP #7 (2026-04-29): renamed from `scope` to disambiguate from consent.scope (a free-string used by consent policies).

promoted_to_backpack.description: Optional Backpack key this Hoard item was promoted into. Lets renderers walk back from carry-state to source.

summary.description: Short summary used by retrieval and renderers.

embedding_ref.description: Optional pointer to a vector index entry for similarity search.

redactions.description: Names of redacted spans (e.g. 'pii', 'health'). The redacted text is removed from content; this field records what was removed and why.
